newsitem.title: ANGOLA: BRAZILIAN LEADER IN FIRST OFFICIAL VISIT TO ANGOLA.
newsitem.headline: BRAZILIAN LEADER IN FIRST OFFICIAL VISIT TO ANGOLA.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso arrived in the Angolan capital Luanda on Sunday for his first official visit to the country.

Cardosa, accompanied by a large government and military delegation, was met at Luanda's International Airport by Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura and United Nations mediator to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye.

He made no comments and was immediately taken to the presidential palace outside Luanda for a meeting with the Brazilian community living in Angola, the southern African country tied to Brazil through the Portuguese language.

On Monday, Cardosa will meet Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos for talks and they are expected to sign a cooperation aagrement. Hours later he is due to fly to the war-torn town of Cuito in Bie province where he will meet Brazilian peacekeepers helping to implement a two-year-old peace accord on the ground.
Cordosa heads to South Africa on Monday evening, the first visit to the country by a Brazilian leader.
Cardoso's three-day visit is aimed at defrosting decades of icy relations that resulted from Brazil's vigorous opposition to South Africa's former policy of apartheid, diplomats said.
He will meet President Nelson Mandela on Tuesday. The two leaders are expected to sign several accords including an agreement to protect investments.
South African foreign direct investment in Brazil totals some $1.0 billion, with both sides hoping greater investor security will double that sum over the next four years.
